Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Demak Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Demak.
4. Regional Apparatus Working Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in Demak Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
11. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
12. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community, including children who become perpetrators of violence.
15. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
16. Psychosocial Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems faced
17. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the established operational standards.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 10

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 8 letter a include:

a. conducting communication, information, and education about gender-based violence and violence against children; and
b. socialization of laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and violence against children.

I. GENERAL

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, therefore they must be protected and their honor, dignity, and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class in community life, nationhood and statehood.

To achieve the enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children which is set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children in the form of policies applicable both at the national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations or conflicts. Acts of violence against women and children are actions that violate, hinder, eliminate and ignore the human rights of women and the rights of children.

7. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
11. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
12. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community, including children who become perpetrators of violence.
15. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
16. Psychosocial Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems faced
17. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the established operational standards.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and Regency/City as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of Integrated Service System development, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Demak Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Demak.
4. Regional Apparatus Working Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in Demak Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
11. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
12. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community, including children who become perpetrators of violence.
15. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
16. Psychosocial Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems faced
17. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the established operational standards.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, therefore they must be protected and their honor, dignity, and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class in community life, nationhood and statehood.

To achieve the enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children which is set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children in the form of policies applicable both at the national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations or conflicts. Acts of violence against women and children are actions that violate, hinder, eliminate and ignore the human rights of women and the rights of children.

letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture, and language, legal status and physical or mental condition. letter b What is meant by "best interests of the child" is all actions concerning child victims of violence carried out by the government, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration letter c What is meant by "life" is the most fundamental human right for children protected by the state, government, society, family and parents.

What is meant by "survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, covering the right to identity.

What is meant by "child development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, covering the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate. letter d What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives. letter e What is meant by "confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the victim's life and psychological well-being. letter f What is meant by "Empowerment" is every action to motivate victims to be able to control their own lives to shape their future according to their wishes. letter g What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced by them. letter h What is meant by "Decision in the hands of the victim" is the right of victims of gender-based violence to determine the best choice in resolving their problems. letter i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, spiritual counselors, social workers, police.

Article 3

The objectives of protection of victims of gender-based violence and children include: a. providing a sense of security for victims;

b. obtaining legal handling; and

c. seeking recovery and social reintegration.

Article 20

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 2

Protection of victims of gender-based violence and children is based on Pancasila and grounded in the 1945 Constitution, as well as basic principles that include:

a. Non-discrimination
b. Best interests of the child
c. Right to life, survival and development
d. Respect for the views of the child
e. Confidentiality
f. Empowerment
g. Not blaming the victim
h. Decision in the hands of the victim
i. Integration

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND VIOLENCE AGAINST CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, therefore they must be protected and their honor, dignity, and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class in community life, nationhood and statehood.

To achieve the enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children which is set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children in the form of policies applicable both at the national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations or conflicts. Acts of violence against women and children are actions that violate, hinder, eliminate and ignore the human rights of women and the rights of children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Part Six

Legal Protection

Article 17

(1) In organizing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the regional government shall cooperate with the Central Government, Provincial Government and Regency/City Government and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Central Government and Provincial Government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include consultation, coordination and reporting.

(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and Regency/City as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of Integrated Service System development, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Demak Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Demak.
4. Regional Apparatus Working Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in Demak Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
11. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
12. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community, including children who become perpetrators of violence.
15. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
16. Psychosocial Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems faced
17. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the established operational standards.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 18

(1) The Regent shall conduct control, guidance and supervision of the organization of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children.

(2) The implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out on a daily basis by the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Article 20

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 3

The objectives of protection of victims of gender-based violence and children include: a. providing a sense of security for victims;

b. obtaining legal handling; and

c. seeking recovery and social reintegration.

Article 10

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 8 letter a include:

a. conducting communication, information, and education about gender-based violence and violence against children; and
b. socialization of laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and violence against children.

I. GENERAL

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, therefore they must be protected and their honor, dignity, and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class in community life, nationhood and statehood.

To achieve the enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children which is set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children in the form of policies applicable both at the national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations or conflicts. Acts of violence against women and children are actions that violate, hinder, eliminate and ignore the human rights of women and the rights of children.

Article 17

(1) In organizing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the regional government shall cooperate with the Central Government, Provincial Government and Regency/City Government and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Central Government and Provincial Government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include consultation, coordination and reporting.

(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and Regency/City as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of Integrated Service System development, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Demak Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Demak.
4. Regional Apparatus Working Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in Demak Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
11. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
12. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community, including children who become perpetrators of violence.
15. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
16. Psychosocial Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems faced
17. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the established operational standards.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, therefore they must be protected and their honor, dignity, and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class in community life, nationhood and statehood.

To achieve the enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children which is set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children in the form of policies applicable both at the national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations or conflicts. Acts of violence against women and children are actions that violate, hinder, eliminate and ignore the human rights of women and the rights of children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

Protection of victims of gender-based violence and children is based on Pancasila and grounded in the 1945 Constitution, as well as basic principles that include:

a. Non-discrimination
b. Best interests of the child
c. Right to life, survival and development
d. Respect for the views of the child
e. Confidentiality
f. Empowerment
g. Not blaming the victim
h. Decision in the hands of the victim
i. Integration

Article 2

letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture, and language, legal status and physical or mental condition. letter b What is meant by "best interests of the child" is all actions concerning child victims of violence carried out by the government, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration letter c What is meant by "life" is the most fundamental human right for children protected by the state, government, society, family and parents.

What is meant by "survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, covering the right to identity.

What is meant by "child development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, covering the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate. letter d What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives. letter e What is meant by "confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the victim's life and psychological well-being. letter f What is meant by "Empowerment" is every action to motivate victims to be able to control their own lives to shape their future according to their wishes. letter g What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced by them. letter h What is meant by "Decision in the hands of the victim" is the right of victims of gender-based violence to determine the best choice in resolving their problems. letter i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, spiritual counselors, social workers, police.

Article 20

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 10

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 8 letter a include:

a. conducting communication, information, and education about gender-based violence and violence against children; and
b. socialization of laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and violence against children.

Article 3

The objectives of protection of victims of gender-based violence and children include: a. providing a sense of security for victims;

b. obtaining legal handling; and

c. seeking recovery and social reintegration.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Demak Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Demak.
4. Regional Apparatus Working Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in Demak Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
11. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
12. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community, including children who become perpetrators of violence.
15. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
16. Psychosocial Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems faced
17. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the established operational standards.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

11. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
12. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

14. 16. Psychosocial Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems faced
17. I. GENERAL

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, therefore they must be protected and their honor, dignity, and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class in community life, nationhood and statehood.

To achieve the enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children which is set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children in the form of policies applicable both at the national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations or conflicts. Acts of violence against women and children are actions that violate, hinder, eliminate and ignore the human rights of women and the rights of children.

To achieve the enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children which is set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations or conflicts. Acts of violence against women and children are actions that violate, hinder, eliminate and ignore the human rights of women and the rights of children.

14. letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture, and language, legal status and physical or mental condition. letter b What is meant by "best interests of the child" is all actions concerning child victims of violence carried out by the government, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration letter c What is meant by "life" is the most fundamental human right for children protected by the state, government, society, family and parents.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND VIOLENCE AGAINST CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, therefore they must be protected and their honor, dignity, and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class in community life, nationhood and statehood.

To achieve the enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children which is set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children in the form of policies applicable both at the national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations or conflicts. Acts of violence against women and children are actions that violate, hinder, eliminate and ignore the human rights of women and the rights of children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 17

(1) In organizing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the regional government shall cooperate with the Central Government, Provincial Government and Regency/City Government and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Central Government and Provincial Government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include consultation, coordination and reporting.

(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and Regency/City as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of Integrated Service System development, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

Article 7

(1) The integrated service as referred to in Article 6 shall be established by the Regional Government in accordance with the laws and regulations. (2) The establishment of integrated service as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of members from regional government elements, non-governmental institutions, health service institutions, law enforcement apparatus, professional personnel, companion volunteers, social workers, religious counselors, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

(3) The Service Operational Standards (SOP) for Integrated Services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER II

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Demak Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Demak.
4. Regional Apparatus Working Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in Demak Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
11. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
12. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community, including children who become perpetrators of violence.
15. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
16. Psychosocial Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems faced
17. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the established operational standards.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS AND AUTHORITIES OF THE REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 2

Protection of victims of gender-based violence and children is based on Pancasila and grounded in the 1945 Constitution, as well as basic principles that include:

a. Non-discrimination
b. Best interests of the child
c. Right to life, survival and development
d. Respect for the views of the child
e. Confidentiality
f. Empowerment
g. Not blaming the victim
h. Decision in the hands of the victim
i. Integration

Article 2

letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture, and language, legal status and physical or mental condition. letter b What is meant by "best interests of the child" is all actions concerning child victims of violence carried out by the government, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration letter c What is meant by "life" is the most fundamental human right for children protected by the state, government, society, family and parents.

What is meant by "survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, covering the right to identity.

What is meant by "child development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, covering the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate. letter d What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives. letter e What is meant by "confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the victim's life and psychological well-being. letter f What is meant by "Empowerment" is every action to motivate victims to be able to control their own lives to shape their future according to their wishes. letter g What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced by them. letter h What is meant by "Decision in the hands of the victim" is the right of victims of gender-based violence to determine the best choice in resolving their problems. letter i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, spiritual counselors, social workers, police.
